model: Earnings-based cost-of-equity FCFE DCF (bank-like lender; engine route, retention = NI growth / ROE, net debt zero)

inputs.sbc_source: not separately deducted -- SBC is already inside GAAP net income and the engine's ebitda_margin_path is a NET (post-financing, post-credit-cost) margin, not an EBITDA margin; sbc_pct_path held at 0 to avoid double-charging.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, not WACC -- net_debt is held at 0 because AXP's debt and deposits fund its ~$214B card-loan receivables book (operating funding for a lender), not leverage against the fee/network business. Base 10.5% reflects AXP's beta (~1.2-1.3, real if currently-benign consumer-credit cyclicality) against a large-cap US equity risk premium; bull 9.5% / bear 12.0% bracket credit-cycle-dependent risk.
inputs.lease_treatment: not applicable -- lease charges immaterial versus the credit/funding items driving this model (lease_cost_pct_path held at 0)
inputs.notes: Routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md: AXP carries a ~$214B card-loan portfolio and net interest income ~18% of FY2025 revenue -- reported OCF/FCF is dominated by loan originations/collections and total_debt mostly funds the receivables book, so a plain owner-FCF DCF (FCF/WACC with net debt subtracted) would misstate both the flow and the bridge. Modeled instead as an earnings-based FCFE-at-cost-of-equity DCF via the standard component ENGINE (not a hand-built JSON): ebitda_margin_path is set to the projected NET margin (cash_tax_rate_path held at 0, since GAAP net income is already post-tax and post-financing) and capex_pct_path stands in for capital retained to fund loan-book/balance-sheet growth at the assumed ROE (retention_ratio = NI_growth/ROE, capped [0,0.9]; capex_pct = retention_ratio x net_margin), so nopat - capex = NI x (1 - retention) = FCFE -- exactly the mechanic NAB.AX's Drivers.json uses (see NAB.AX_Drivers.json assumptions.base.capex_rationale). Same model family as NAB.AX (FCFE-at-CoE), SOFI (earnings-based bank DCF), SRBK (residual income on tangible book), IAG.AX (FCFE-at-CoE on NEP). FY2025 net income $10,833m is the FY0 anchor; TTM (Q3-25 through Q2-26) net income is $11,446m on revenue $43,086m (~26.6% net margin), consistent with FY2026 guidance (EPS $17.30-17.90, revenue +~10%) implying FY2026 NI ~$11.86-11.9bn at ~26.1% margin -- the base-case Y1 anchor. ROE is ~33-34% TTM (management cited 36.4% for Q2-2026 annualized), far above the ~10.5% cost of equity, so most net income is genuinely distributable via buybacks even while the balance sheet keeps growing -- this matches AXP's actual capital-light buyback behavior (~$5.8bn FY2025, accelerating to $4.2bn in H1-2026 alone, ~4-5%/yr net share count decline). Terminal value uses an exit-P/E cap (16x base) rather than relying on the Gordon growth spread, since a bank/lender's terminal multiple is the more defensible anchor -- versus AXP's own current ~17.6x forward / ~18.3x TTM multiple, itself already compressed from ~25x at the Dec-2025 high per Sept-2026 press coverage, so 16x is flat-to-below today's already-de-rated multiple, not an aggressive re-rating assumption.

historical_growth.notes: 5yr figures (revenue 13.5%, EPS 32.5%) are inflated by the FY2020 COVID trough as the low base (net income fell to $3.1B in FY2020 from $6.9B FY2018) -- 3yr CAGRs (FY2022-FY2025) are the cleaner read: revenue 6.5%, net income 13.0%, EPS 16.0% (buyback-boosted vs NI), equity 10.6%. FCF CAGR is not computed -- owner FCF is not a meaningful concept for a lender whose OCF is dominated by loan-book originations/collections (see inputs.notes); this model does not use it.

base.growth_rationale: Revenue (net revenues). FY2026 10.0% = management's raised FY2026 guide (from ~9-10%, Q2-2026 call) after four straight quarters of double-digit growth. Decelerates toward a 5.0% long-run rate as the Sept-2025 Platinum refresh ($695->$895 fee) and premium mix-shift tailwind (net card fees +15.4% YoY Q2-2026, 70%+ of 2025 new accounts fee-paying) normalizes and billed-business growth reverts toward nominal-GDP-plus-premium-mix trend.
base.margin_rationale: NET margin (post-tax; cash_tax_rate_path held at 0 so ebitda_margin_path IS net margin -- AXP's GAAP net income already nets financing/credit costs, unlike an operating company's EBITDA). FY2026 26.1% = TTM (Q3-25 to Q2-26) actual 26.6% net margin, held near guidance (EPS $17.30-17.90 on ~10% revenue growth implies FY2026 NI ~$11.86-11.9bn, ~26.1% margin). Drifts up modestly to 27.0% as the high-margin net-card-fee line (currently ~12% of revenue, guided to exit 2026 at a high-teens growth rate) keeps outgrowing discount revenue.
base.capex_rationale: capex_pct_path stands in for capital RETAINED to fund balance-sheet/loan-book growth at the assumed ROE, not physical capex -- same mechanic as NAB.AX's Drivers file. retention_ratio = NI_growth / ROE (capped [0,0.9]); capex_pct = retention_ratio x net_margin, expressed as % of revenue, so nopat - capex = NI x (1 - retention) = FCFE. ROE fades from TTM's ~33-34% (management cited 36.4% for Q2-2026 annualized) toward a still-elevated 26% long-run as the ~$214B card-loan book matures and rate tailwinds normalize; retention runs ~5-8% of revenue (payout ~72-81% of NI), consistent with AXP's actual buyback pace (~$5.8bn FY2025, accelerating to $4.2bn in H1-2026 alone, ~4-5%/yr net share count decline).

bull.growth_rationale: Card-fee acceleration (high-teens exit-rate 2026 guidance) sustains into a durable low-teens revenue growth path via continued premium mix-shift and Millennial/Gen-Z account growth (now ~65-75% of new acquisitions, Gen Z US billed business +38% YoY); TheFork/Resy/Tock dining-platform network adds a modest incremental growth lever. Decelerates to a 5.8% terminal.
bull.margin_rationale: Margin expands further (26.3% -> 28.2%) on operating leverage and continued fee-revenue mix shift beyond the base case.
bull.capex_rationale: Same retention mechanic as base; ROE stays elevated near 33-34% (vs base's fade to 26%) and buybacks continue at an aggressive ~4.5%/yr pace, so retention stays in a similar 6-10% of revenue band despite faster NI growth.

bear.growth_rationale: Consumer discretionary/travel spend slows under macro pressure (inflation, elevated gas prices -- both flagged in Sept-2026 press coverage as current headwinds; EPS growth already decelerated from 18% Q1-2026 to 11% Q2-2026), revenue growth drops to mid-single digits and stays there.
bear.margin_rationale: Credit normalizes off currently-benign levels (30+ day delinquency 1.2%, net write-off rate 2.2% per Q2-2026 guidance) as the cycle turns, pushing loan-loss provisions higher and compressing net margin from ~24% toward a trough ~21.7% -- still profitable (AXP's premium, high-spend cardholder base is more resilient than a subprime issuer) but a real credit-cost step-up versus base.
bear.capex_rationale: ROE falls toward 20% as the credit cycle turns and provisions rise; retention stays low (near-zero in Y1-2 as NI actually contracts, then rising modestly) since management preserves capital and buyback pace slows to ~1.5-2%/yr rather than funding loan growth through a downturn.

scenario_narratives.base: Revenue growth decelerates from the FY2026 guided ~10% toward a ~5% long-run rate as card-fee tailwinds (Platinum refresh, premium mix-shift) mature; net margin drifts up modestly (26.1% -> 27.0%) as the high-margin net-card-fee line keeps outgrowing discount revenue; ROE fades gradually from ~33% toward a still-high 26% as the loan book matures and rate tailwinds normalize; buybacks continue near the current ~4-5%/yr pace, moderating to ~1.5%/yr by year 10; discounted at 10.5% cost of equity; exit at 16x year-10 net income, roughly in line with today's already-compressed forward multiple.
scenario_narratives.bull: Card-fee acceleration (high-teens exit-rate 2026 guidance) sustains into a durable double-digit revenue growth path via continued premium mix-shift and Millennial/Gen-Z account growth (now ~65-75% of new acquisitions); margin expands further on operating leverage and fee-revenue mix; ROE stays elevated near 33-34%; buybacks continue at an aggressive ~4.5%/yr pace; the market re-rates the stock back toward its Dec-2025 cycle-high multiple (exit 19x) as growth durability is proven out.
scenario_narratives.bear: Consumer discretionary/travel spend slows under macro pressure (inflation, elevated gas prices), credit normalizes off currently-benign levels (delinquency 1.2%, write-offs 2.2%) pushing provisions higher and compressing margin from ~26% toward ~21.7%; ROE falls toward 20% as the credit cycle turns; buyback pace slows to ~1.5-2%/yr as management preserves capital; multiple stays de-rated at 12x exit, below today's already-compressed level, reflecting a market pricing in a harder landing than currently guided.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 25/50/25. Not skewed further: AXP carries real macro-cyclicality (consumer discretionary spend, travel/dining skew, credit-normalization risk -- EPS growth already decelerating 18% Q1-2026 to 11% Q2-2026, inflation/gas prices flagged as current headwinds) that argues against a rosier weighting, but the balance sheet carries no refinancing risk (net_debt=0 in this model; deposits/debt fund a $214B card-loan book against ROE ~33-34%, stable delinquency 1.2% and net write-offs 2.2% per Q2-2026 guidance) that argues against a heavier bear weighting either.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Earnings-based FCFE-at-cost-of-equity model for a card issuer/network with material on-balance-sheet lending -- not an owner-FCF WACC DCF. Net income is the flow; FCFE = NI less the retention needed to fund balance-sheet/capital growth at the assumed ROE (modeled via the engine's capex_pct_path, same mechanic as NAB.AX); discounted at cost of equity; net_debt held at zero because deposits/debt fund the loan receivables book, not leverage against the network/fee business. See inputs.notes for the full routing rationale and folder precedent (NAB.AX, SOFI, SRBK, IAG.AX).
key_risks_to_valuation: Consumer credit-cycle turn: delinquency/write-offs are currently benign (1.2%/2.2%) but AXP's premium-skew book is not immune to a harder macro landing
Card-fee growth deceleration if the Platinum refresh tailwind fades faster than guided
Multiple de-rating already underway (per Sept-2026 coverage, ~25x to ~18x TTM P/E in under a year) could continue rather than stabilize
TheFork and other bolt-on M&A (pending $700M) diverting capital from buybacks, slowing the per-share compounding this model relies on
Regulatory/interchange risk to discount revenue (56% of FY2025 revenue) is not separately modeled
